rv.q: It’s hard to get the genre’s balance of harrowing realism and crude joys right on stage. And as funny as this show’s offbeat animal puppets and showboating song-and-dance moments are, they sit weirdly alongside the story’s nihilistic trajectory. … what Jamie Eastlake’s production really does nail is the humour.
It's frustratingly scattershot, and just about hangs together thanks to the sheer energy of its execution.
